# Module 5: Common Numerical Failure Modes

## Module Arc

- Cancellation loses significant information
- Reductions accumulate rounding
- Intermediate range matters
- Stable reformulations preserve useful information

::: notes
This module should be experiment-heavy. Use several small failures rather than
one long implementation.
:::

## Diagnose The Pattern

- Subtracting nearly equal quantities
- Mixing very large and very small magnitudes
- Overflow before a representable final result
- Underflow in products or probabilities
- Strong dependence on evaluation order

::: notes
Ask participants to name the dangerous operation before showing an improved
formulation.
:::

## Summation Is An Algorithm

- Naive sequential order
- Magnitude-aware order
- Pairwise reduction
- Compensated summation
- Accuracy, cost, and parallelism trade-offs

::: notes
Use the same input for every method and compare against a stronger reference.
:::
